name: Tanning wipes / towelettes

card.summary: Pre-soaked DHA wipes for quick self-tan application; temporary colour with no published clinical trials.
card.note: Colour is temporary and can streak; DHA is not approved for use around eyes or lips.

quick.overview:
Tanning wipes are pre-moistened cloths impregnated with a self-tanning composition, such as DHA, that are wiped over the skin for convenience.

A patent filing describes the concept, but no clinical studies of the product category were found.
quick.mechanism: Wipes deliver the same kind of DHA colour as other self-tanners, which reacts with the dead outer skin layer and fades in about 3 to 10 days.[1]
quick.risks: Uneven wiping can cause streaking or orange colour, and DHA is not approved around eyes, lips or mucous membranes.[1] Bronzers may rub off on clothing.[1]

lead: Tanning wipes, or towelettes, are tissues pre-soaked with a self-tanning or bronzing composition for application by wiping. A patent filing describes a tanning aid made of tissue paper impregnated with a tanning lotion, tanning oil or bronzing agent.[2]
Self-tanning products commonly use DHA, which colours the dead outer layer of skin without UV and fades within roughly 3 to 10 days.[1]
No clinical studies on tanning wipes were found.

paras: A patented concept pairs a tissue with an impregnated tanning lotion, oil or bronzing agent, wiped over the body surface.[2] Wikipedia's sunless tanning article lists creams, lotions, sprays, bronzers and gradual tanners but not wipes.[1]
DHA reacts with amino acids in the dead outer skin layer in a browning reaction, independent of UV and melanin.[1]

Improper application is reported to produce orange or splotchy colour.[1] The FDA has approved DHA for external use but not near the eyes, lips or mucous membranes.[1] Skin may be more UV-susceptible for about 24 hours after DHA application.[1]
